subject: science
question_text: State the Universal law of gravitation?
answer_text: According to Universal Law of Gravitation, every object in the universe attracts every other object with a force known as Gravitational force.
final_answer: Thus, every object attracts every other object with a gravitational force.

subject: science
question_text: What do you mean by free fall?
answer_text: Gravity of earth attracts every object towards its center. When an object is dropped from a certain height, it begins to fall towards Earth’s surface under the influence of gravitational force. Such a motion of the object is called free fall.
final_answer: Therefore, free fall is the motion of an object falling under the influence of gravity.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of gravitational effects on falling objects.

subject: science
question_text: What do you mean by acceleration due to gravity?
answer_text: When an object falls freely towards the surface of earth from a certain height, then its velocity changes. This change in velocity produces acceleration in the object which is known as acceleration due to gravity denoted by the letter g. The value of acceleration due to gravity is g.
final_answer: Thus, acceleration due to gravity is the acceleration experienced by an object in free fall.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the concept of acceleration in free fall.

subject: science
question_text: What are the differences between mass of an object and its weight?
answer_text:
Mass:
1. Mass is the quantity of matter contained in the body.
2. It is the measure of inertia of the body.
3. It is a constant quantity for any object.
4. It is a scalar quantity and only has magnitude.
5. SI unit of mass is Kg.

Weight:
1. Weight is the gravitational force acting on the body.
2. It is the measure of gravity.
3. Weight of an object is not a constant quantity; it is different at different places.
final_answer: In summary, mass is a measure of matter, while weight is the force of gravity on that matter.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of two fundamental concepts in physics.

subject: science
question_text: Why is the weight of an object on the moon (1/6)th its weight on the earth?
answer_text: Gravity is directly related to mass. The more mass an object has, the more gravitational pull it has. Now, the moon is significantly smaller than the earth (in fact, it is about the size of the earth’s core). Gravity is dependent on the size of the object. Your weight on the moon is 1/6 of that on earth because the moon has 1/6 the mass of the earth.
final_answer: Thus, the weight on the moon is 1/6 of that on earth due to the moon's smaller mass.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of gravitational force and mass relationship.

subject: science
question_text: Why is it difficult to hold a school bag having a strap made of a thin and strong string?
answer_text: It is difficult to hold a school bag having a thin strap because the pressure on the shoulders is quite large. This is because the pressure is inversely proportional to the surface area on which the force acts. The smaller the surface area, the larger the pressure on the surface. In the case of a thin strap, the contact surface area is very small. Hence, the pressure exerted on the shoulder is very large.
final_answer: Therefore, the thin strap causes high pressure on the shoulders due to its small surface area.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of pressure and surface area relationship.

subject: science
question_text: What do you mean by buoyancy?
answer_text: The upward force exerted by a liquid on an object that is immersed in it is known as buoyancy.
final_answer: Thus, buoyancy is the upward force acting on immersed objects.

subject: science
question_text: Why does an object float or sink when placed on the surface of water?
answer_text: If the density of an object is more than the density of the liquid, then the object would sink. This happens because in this case, the buoyant force acting on the object due to the liquid is less than the force of gravity acting on the object. If the density of the object is less than the density of the liquid, then it floats on the surface of the liquid. This happens because the buoyant force acting on the object is greater than the force of gravity.
final_answer: Therefore, an object sinks if it is denser than the liquid and floats if it is less dense.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of density and buoyant force.

subject: science
question_text: You find your mass to be 42 Kg on a weighing machine. Is your weight more or less than 42 Kg?
answer_text: On a weighing machine, mass is measured by comparing the weights. So when you weigh your body, an upward force (buoyant force) acts on it, which causes the machine to show your weight less than the actual weight.
final_answer: Thus, your weight is less than 42 Kg due to the buoyant force acting on you.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of buoyant force and weight measurement.

subject: science
question_text: You have a bag of cotton and an iron bar, each indicating a mass of 100 Kg when measured on a weighing machine. In reality, one is heavier than the other. Can you say which one is heavier and why?
answer_text: Actual weight of any object is equal to the sum of its measured weight and the buoyant force. The bag of cotton is heavier since it is larger than the iron bar, so the buoyant force is larger in the case of cotton. Hence, the actual weight of the cotton bag is more and it is heavier.
final_answer: Therefore, the bag of cotton is heavier than the iron bar due to the larger buoyant force acting on it.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of buoyant force and weight comparison.
